title: Principles and Sources of Unitarian Universalism (1985–2024)
attributionNote: A statement adopted through UUA congregational processes, not a scripture. In 2024 Unitarian Universalists adopted Shared Values language; the older Six Sources formulation remains historically important but is not the current statement.
description: The Principles and Sources expressed a historically specific Unitarian Universalist self-description, including affirmations of inherent worth, justice, spiritual growth and the use of multiple sources. It should be read with its date and institutional provenance.
historicalContext: The statement was revised over several decades and reflects the pluralistic character of Unitarian Universalism. Its sources explicitly include direct experience, prophetic traditions, world religions, humanism and Earth-centred spirituality.
availabilityNote: Catalogue record only. UUA site terms prohibit distribution or derivative works without written permission. The official UUA page is linked from the source registry.
